positions.reasons: TABRISI (author): The circumstantial phrase is governed by أتجعل فيها من يفسد; باء in بحمدك attaches to نسبح and لام in لك to نقدس.

positions.position: Al-Tabari, citing Abu Rawq, says jaʿil here means “creator”; its single object supports this.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (الطبري): Al-Tabari, citing Abu Rawq, says jaʿil here means “creator”; its single object supports this.

positions.position: جاعل from جعل takes two objects, here في الأرض and خليفة, because it is future and depends on a subject; it can also mean ‘creator.’
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): جاعل from جعل takes two objects, here في الأرض and خليفة, because it is future and depends on a subject; it can also mean ‘creator.’

positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Jāʿil is an active participle with future force; if it governs its object, that is better than annexation for Sibawayh, while al-Kisāʾī considers both equal and Abū Ḥayyān prefers annexation.

positions.position: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة is the quoted content and direct object of قال; إن is closed because it follows قال without a meaning of supposition.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة is the quoted content and direct object of قال; إن is closed because it follows قال without a meaning of supposition.

positions.position: If جاعل means خالق, خليفة is its object and في الأرض either attaches to جاعل or is an omitted phrase circumstantially modifying the following indefinite noun.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): If جاعل means خالق, خليفة is its object and في الأرض either attaches to جاعل or is an omitted phrase circumstantially modifying the following indefinite noun.

positions.position: Al-Zamakhshari takes جاعل to mean صير, making خليفة the first object and في الأرض the fronted second object.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhshari takes جاعل to mean صير, making خليفة the first object and في الأرض the fronted second object.

positions.position: خليفة is accusative as the object of جاعل; active participles govern like their verbs and may be annexed to their object for lightness if nothing intervenes.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): خليفة is accusative as the object of جاعل; active participles govern like their verbs and may be annexed to their object for lightness if nothing intervenes.

positions.position: If تجعل means create, the first فيها is attached to it and من يفسد is its object.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): If تجعل means create, the first فيها is attached to it and من يفسد is its object.

positions.position: If تجعل means make into, the first فيها is its second object, advanced before من يفسد.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): If تجعل means make into, the first فيها is its second object, advanced before من يفسد.

positions.position: A statement may be emphatically confirmed even when its audience has no doubt, as in God's declaration إني جاعل, strengthened by inna and the active participle.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (author): A statement may be emphatically confirmed even when its audience has no doubt, as in God's declaration إني جاعل, strengthened by inna and the active participle.

positions.position: Jāʿil can mean “making into,” taking khalīfa and “in the earth” as two objects; or “creating,” with one object and “in the earth” modifying khalīfa.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): Jāʿil can mean “making into,” taking khalīfa and “in the earth” as two objects; or “creating,” with one object and “in the earth” modifying khalīfa.

positions.position: The word jaʿil may mean create: when jaʿl takes one object it means creation, and here it is broader and more general than khalq while allowing both senses.

question: What does “the earth” denote here?

positions.position: The earth here is Mecca
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): A report places the earth's spreading from Mecca, the House and prophets' graves there. MAWARDI-FULL (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): Ibn Sābiṭ reports the Prophet said that the earth was spread out from Mecca. MAWARDI-FULL (author): The text says this is why Mecca was called Umm al-Qurā, and locates the graves of Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, and Shuʿayb between Zamzam, the Corner, and the Station. IBNATIYYA-FULL (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): A report from the Prophet says “the earth” here means Mecca, from beneath which earth was spread; it was where prophets’ peoples were destroyed, and Noah’s, Hud’s, and Salih’s graves lie between the Station and the Corner. TABRISI (النبي): The Prophet is cited as saying that the earth was spread out from Mecca, which is why it is called the Mother of Towns. RAZI-FULL (author): Razi judges the whole-earth interpretation closer to the apparent wording than the Mecca report. QURTUBI-FULL (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): Ibn Sabit reports that the earth was spread from Mecca, called Umm al-Qura, and that Noah, Hud, Salih, and Shuʿayb are buried between Zamzam and the Corner and Station. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (الجمهور): The apparent sense of fī al-arḍ is the whole earth, as the majority hold; another view identifies the land as Mecca. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (ابن سابط): Ibn Sābiṭ transmits the Mecca interpretation as a report traced to the Prophet; Abū Ḥayyān says it should be followed if authentic. ALUSI-FULL (الجمهور): The majority take “the earth” to mean the whole earth; another view identifies it as Mecca, based on a report attributed to the Prophet that the author considers probably unsound. TABRISI (author): A view takes الأرض as Mecca, citing its being the first land spread and a report about prophets' graves there; the author prefers the apparent, known earth. IBNKATHIR-FULL (author): Ibn Kathir grades that report mursal with a weak chain and an inserted interpretation that “earth” means Mecca; he says the apparent sense is the wider earth.

positions.position: The earth means the whole earth
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): The earth most naturally means all the earth from east to west.

question: Why is the earth specified for the successor?

positions.position: Another account says the passage gathers evidence for divine unity from earth and heaven, then follows with the beginning of creation and Adam.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): Another account says the passage gathers evidence for divine unity from earth and heaven, then follows with the beginning of creation and Adam.

positions.position: Another explanation says the announcement taught Adam he was created for earthly life, not Paradise; the angels sought the wisdom of that arrangement.
positions.reasons: TABRISI (author): Another explanation says the announcement taught Adam he was created for earthly life, not Paradise; the angels sought the wisdom of that arrangement.

positions.position: The four terms form earthly and heavenly pairs, with the soul positioned between them; corruption and sanctification are the far ends, and the middle terms bridge earth and heaven.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (author): The four terms form earthly and heavenly pairs, with the soul positioned between them; corruption and sanctification are the far ends, and the middle terms bridge earth and heaven.

positions.position: Mentioning earth signals that earth angels challenged Adam; heavenly angels administer the upper world, while earth angels envied the caliphate and their own dominion.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): Mentioning earth signals that earth angels challenged Adam; heavenly angels administer the upper world, while earth angels envied the caliphate and their own dominion.

positions.position: Earth is specified because it is the realm of change and transformation, where the effects of all divine names sought by God become manifest, unlike the higher realm.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): Earth is specified because it is the realm of change and transformation, where the effects of all divine names sought by God become manifest, unlike the higher realm.

positions.position: They reason that the successor's purpose is to glorify and sanctify God, but earthly life draws the human toward evil; they claim angels already fulfill that purpose and ask why appoint a human.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): They reason that the successor's purpose is to glorify and sanctify God, but earthly life draws the human toward evil; they claim angels already fulfill that purpose and ask why appoint a human.

question: What does khalīfa mean and how is it formed?

positions.position: Khalīfa denotes one who succeeds another
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Khalifa denotes succeeding another, with 10:14 and rulers as examples. TAB-FULL (author): Khalifa denotes succeeding another, with 10:14 and rulers as examples. TAB-FULL (author): Khalifa denotes succeeding another, with 10:14 and rulers as examples. NAHHAS (author): «خليفة» may be active: one who succeeds the angels or other predecessors in the earth, as also related. NAHHAS (author): Alternatively «خليفة» may be passive, one who is succeeded. THALABI (author): Khalifa means a replacement for those before, succeeding them after they depart. MAWARDI-FULL (author): With fatḥa, khalaf denotes righteous successors and with sukūn, wicked successors; the Qur’an and a hadith illustrate the distinction. JISHUMI (author): Khalaf with fatḥa on the lām denotes righteous successors, while sukūn denotes bad successors, as illustrated in 7:169. IBNATIYYA-FULL (author): Khalīfa means one who succeeds another. IBNJAWZI-ZAD (ابن الأنباري): Khalīfa means one who succeeds another; Ibn al-Anbārī says its original form was khalīf, with the feminine ending added to intensify praise, like ʿallāma and nasāba. QURTUBI-FULL (author): Khalifa as an active noun is a successor to angels or other earlier beings; as a passive noun, it means one made a successor. QURTUBI-FULL (author): Khalaf with a vowel refers to righteous successors, while the still form refers to wicked ones. BAYDAWI-FULL (author): خليفة is one who succeeds or represents another, with its feminine ending marking intensification. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (الجمهور): The majority read khalīfa with fāʾ; it can mean an active successor or one replaced, and in the active sense one entrusted to act in another's place. SAMIN-DURR (author): خليفة can mean an active successor, succeeding the people addressed or the jinn who preceded them; this is stronger because its feminine suffix is regular for the active sense. SAMIN-DURR (author): Alternatively, خليفة means one succeeded by each later generation; the feminine suffix is not regular for this passive sense unless the word has become noun-like, as in النطيحة and الذبيحة. IBNKATHIR-FULL (author): Khalifa here means people succeeding one another generation after generation, as in the linked verses about successors on earth. ALUSI-FULL (author): A khalīfa succeeds another and acts in their place; its feminine ending is intensive, so the term can designate a man. ELMALILI (author): God's appointing His chosen servants as successors is a form of deputation bestowed purely to honor them. KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): Khilāfa means succeeding another, representing that person, or exercising that person's authority. STUDYQURAN (author): In other passages khalīfah means successor, as in 7:69 for successors after Noah’s people; related references include 7:74, 10:14, 10:73, 27:62, and 35:39. NASAFI-FULL (author): Khalīfa means a successor, with a feminine hāʾ for emphasis.

positions.position: The feminine ending of khalīfa intensifies or nominalizes the form
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Khalīfa is on faʿīla, which can be an intensive active form like al-ʿalīm or a passive form like al-naṭīḥa; its tāʾ can intensify. ELMALILI (author): Khalifa is an intensive nominal adjective from khalif, on the faʿīl pattern with the meaning of fāʿil; French représentant conveys the sense, with khalāʾif and khulafāʾ as plurals and khilāfa as the verbal noun.

positions.position: God formed the vicegerent according to prior knowledge, composed his form, clothed him in signs of divine attributes so he might know God, and held his breaths in reserve until their manifestation.
positions.reasons: SULAMI (الواسطي): God formed the vicegerent according to prior knowledge, composed his form, clothed him in signs of divine attributes so he might know God, and held his breaths in reserve until their manifestation.

positions.position: خليفة may be singular or plural and apply to male or female.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): خليفة may be singular or plural and apply to male or female.

positions.position: There is no need to supply an omitted khalifa, since wording without ellipsis is better; the active participle conveys a settled state rather than gradual renewal.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): There is no need to supply an omitted khalifa, since wording without ellipsis is better; the active participle conveys a settled state rather than gradual renewal.

positions.position: Whether jaʿala means create or appoint, Adam became khalifa only once, so the act was not repeated.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Whether jaʿala means create or appoint, Adam became khalifa only once, so the act was not repeated.

positions.position: Under the first three readings, angels' prior knowledge may come from God, the Preserved Tablet, observation of other created beings, analogy with earlier earthly inhabitants, or inference from the word khalifa and its association with injustice.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Under the first three readings, angels' prior knowledge may come from God, the Preserved Tablet, observation of other created beings, analogy with earlier earthly inhabitants, or inference from the word khalifa and its association with injustice.

positions.position: Al-Hasan and Qatada, in Ibn Jarir's report, explain God's statement as informing the angels that He was going to create a khalifa.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (الحسن وقتادة): Al-Hasan and Qatada, in Ibn Jarir's report, explain God's statement as informing the angels that He was going to create a khalifa.

positions.position: Al-Baḥr prefers “creating,” given the contrast; the transformative sense would require an explicit or implied khalīfa.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (البحر): Al-Baḥr prefers “creating,” given the contrast; the transformative sense would require an explicit or implied khalīfa.

positions.position: On the creation reading, “in the earth” modifies khalīfa and is fronted to create anticipation; the active participle works with future sense and dependence on a subject.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): On the creation reading, “in the earth” modifies khalīfa and is fronted to create anticipation; the active participle works with future sense and dependence on a subject.

positions.position: One view takes the khalīfa as Adam and his descendants, supported by the angels' wording; their exchange would then disclose Adam's superiority as the origin of those who follow him.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (قيل): One view takes the khalīfa as Adam and his descendants, supported by the angels' wording; their exchange would then disclose Adam's superiority as the origin of those who follow him.

positions.position: God means that He knows the wisdom in appointing the vicegerent, of which the angels know nothing.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): God means that He knows the wisdom in appointing the vicegerent, of which the angels know nothing.

positions.position: God's making a vicegerent means granting him some divine powers and attributes so that he may exercise delegated authority over creation in God's name.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): God's making a vicegerent means granting him some divine powers and attributes so that he may exercise delegated authority over creation in God's name.

positions.position: The angels may have inferred the possibility of corruption from the title khalifa: vicegerency entails reform and control of those under the vicegerent, but also the possibility of wrongdoing.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): The angels may have inferred the possibility of corruption from the title khalifa: vicegerency entails reform and control of those under the vicegerent, but also the possibility of wrongdoing.

question: Who is the khalīfa?

positions.position: The successor is humanity across generations
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (ابن إسحاق): Ibn Ishaq explains khalifa as a nonangelic inhabitant who settles and cultivates the earth; Adam’s creation was a test, and God had disclosed that his descendants would sin and shed blood. MAWARDI-FULL (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masʿūd says the khalīfa is God’s deputy in judging among creation: Adam and those of his descendants who take his place. TABRISI (author): Another view calls Adam and his descendants successors to the angels who had inhabited earth before them. RAZI-FULL (الحسن): Al-Hasan says the successor is Adam's descendants, who follow one another, supported by the verse about successors on earth. BAYDAWI-FULL (author): Other interpretations take خليفة as a successor to earth’s previous inhabitants, or as Adam together with his descendants succeeding predecessors or one another; the singular may stand for his descendants, ‘one who succeeds you,’ or a collective succession. NASAFI-FULL (author): The khalifa may mean a successor to the angels, who had inhabited earth before Adam and his descendants. SAMIN-DURR (author): The singular خليفة can intend Adam and his descendants collectively, using the ancestor as with tribal names Mudar and Rabi'a; another view understands خليفة as a generic. BIQAI-FULL (author): Adam’s succession extends across the earth through himself and his descendants; the singular khalīfa suits the completeness of this role, though it can also be generic. BIQAI-FULL (author): A khalīfa is one who carries out the predecessor’s work according to that deputy’s rank; humans succeed one another, while Adam is God’s deputy in the realm of dominion. BURSEVI (author): God’s announcement of Adam’s caliphate displays his honor to the angels, so they should revere him rather than reject the human traits shown by him and his descendants.

positions.position: Adam succeeds the earthly angels
positions.reasons: IBNABIHATIM (محمد بن إسحاق): Ibn Ishaq says the khalifa is a being created apart from the angels to dwell in and cultivate the earth. THALABI (author): God knows the benefit in appointing a successor on earth, so the angels should not object to His judgment and governance. JISHUMI (author): The author prefers the interrogative: it asks about the angels’ state relative to the appointment, not whether God will appoint a successor. BAGHAWI-FULL (author): The announced khalifa is a replacement for the angels, whom God will raise up to Him; they disliked this because they had been the least worshipful angels. TABRISI (author): إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة is the object clause of قال; the angels' speech is the object clause of قالوا. IBNJAWZI-ZAD (ابن زيد): Ibn Zayd says the angels feared after God created fire and told them it was for those who disobeyed; they feared they might disobey, so God announced the earthly khalīfa. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Both meanings are possible, but creation is stronger: if the first jaʿala meant appointment, the angels' reply would have explicitly called its object a khalifa. IBNKATHIR-FULL (محمد بن إسحاق): Ibn Ishaq understands the khalifa as an inhabitant and cultivator who will live on and populate earth, a successor unlike the angels. IBNKATHIR-FULL (عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم): God announced that He would create beings and appoint a successor on an otherwise empty earth where only angels existed. ELMALILI (author): The answer says angels do not know the wisdom, motives, and fitness of caliphate; it also implies angelic qualities alone are insufficient and that requesting office is improper.

positions.position: The successor is Adam
positions.reasons: THALABI (بعض الحكماء): A sage argues that Adam was destined to leave paradise before entering it: the earthly successor was announced first, and Adam’s later departure after sin shows divine decree. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): The prophets are God's successors on earth, and Adam alone is named because he is the forefather of all successors, as tribal names can stand for the whole tribe. BURSEVI (author): Adam is called created from clay in reference to his body, but made a caliph in reference to his spirit; this marks his distinction and dignity.

positions.position: Adam is God's appointed deputy
positions.reasons: NASAFI-FULL (author): Alternatively Adam is God’s vicegerent on earth, as every prophet is; the author cites God’s address to David in 38:26. ALUSI-FULL (السادة الصوفية): They say the angel appeared fully in the Muhammadan Reality, as indicated by the revelation of a spirit from God's command; hence Muhammad is creation's supreme and true vicegerent. ALUSI-FULL (الخليفة الأعظم): The report from the supreme vicegerent says God created Adam in His image, or in the image of the Merciful; the author uses it to explain Adam's comprehensiveness. ALUSI-FULL (author): Adam is God's vicegerent in the earth; prophets likewise succeed him in cultivating earth, governing people, perfecting souls, and carrying out God's command, not from divine need. ALUSI-FULL (أهل الله): The people of God identify Adam as God's vicegerent, father of later vicegerents, and comprehensive locus of divine beauty and majesty; both of God's hands are thereby described as right hands. ALUSI-FULL (قيل): Another explanation is that prophets and righteous people will descend from the vicegerent. SAMARRAI-ASRAR (author): Al-Baqara opens the Adam story at its earliest event: before Adam is created, God tells the angels He will appoint a vicegerent on earth. SAMARRAI-ASRAR (author): The story honors Adam through his appointment as earth’s vicegerent, his being taught all the names beyond the angels’ knowledge, and the angels’ prostration to him.

positions.position: Adam succeeds the earlier jinn
positions.reasons: WAHIDI-WAJIZ (author): The khalīfa is Adam, successor to the angels who had inhabited the earth after the jinn; the story recalls the beginning of human creation. BAGHAWI-FULL (قيل): One view identifies the khalifa as Adam because he came after the jinn; another says he is called khalifa because others will succeed him.

positions.position: Al-Hasan says Adam’s children are called successors because each generation follows the preceding one; Ibn Atiyya says this can mean a succeeding or succeeded generation.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (الحسن): Al-Hasan says Adam’s children are called successors because each generation follows the preceding one; Ibn Atiyya says this can mean a succeeding or succeeded generation.

positions.position: Being God’s servant is a greater honor than earthly caliphate: Adam’s caliph title did not deter Satan, but Satan has no power over those God calls His servants.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Being God’s servant is a greater honor than earthly caliphate: Adam’s caliph title did not deter Satan, but Satan has no power over those God calls His servants.

positions.position: Abū Ḥayyān says God singled Adam out by announcing a khalifa, unlike the creation of the heavens, throne, or Paradise, thereby honoring and distinguishing him.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Abū Ḥayyān says God singled Adam out by announcing a khalifa, unlike the creation of the heavens, throne, or Paradise, thereby honoring and distinguishing him.

positions.position: In Ibn ʿAbbās's account, God gave Iblis earthly and lower-heaven sovereignty and Paradise's treasury; pride led him to think he was God's most honored angel, so the announced successor would replace him and his host.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (ابن عباس): In Ibn ʿAbbās's account, God gave Iblis earthly and lower-heaven sovereignty and Paradise's treasury; pride led him to think he was God's most honored angel, so the announced successor would replace him and his host.

positions.position: Al-Ḥasan says the khalifa is Adam's progeny, each generation replacing another; the singular can represent a collective, as in other Qurʾanic passages.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (الحسن): Al-Ḥasan says the khalifa is Adam's progeny, each generation replacing another; the singular can represent a collective, as in other Qurʾanic passages.

positions.position: The second purpose is to honor Adam by announcing his coming to the inhabitants of the divine realm and naming him khalīfa before his creation.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): The second purpose is to honor Adam by announcing his coming to the inhabitants of the divine realm and naming him khalīfa before his creation.

positions.position: One purpose of calling Adam caliph is to show that God graciously accept
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): One purpose of calling Adam caliph is to show that God graciously accepted humanity for servanthood and caliphate, encouraging people not to despair but to continue serving.

positions.position: Hasan takes khalifa as successive generations.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Hasan takes khalifa as successive generations.

positions.position: Ibn Zayd says an empty earth would receive a created khalifa.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Ibn Zayd says an empty earth would receive a created khalifa.

positions.position: On the assertive reading, they may have inferred that a new vicegerent would corrupt the earth because the jinn before them had done so.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI-FULL (author): On the assertive reading, they may have inferred that a new vicegerent would corrupt the earth because the jinn before them had done so.

positions.position: Khalīfa and imām overlap in use, but khalīfa succeeds another while imām leads a group and is to be obeyed.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): Khalīfa and imām overlap in use, but khalīfa succeeds another while imām leads a group and is to be obeyed.

positions.position: The general reading is khalīfa with fāʾ.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (العامة): The general reading is khalīfa with fāʾ.

positions.position: Thaʿlab and others say angels had witnessed the jinn’s corruption and bloodshed, so they asked whether the new successor would follow the jinn’s way.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب): Thaʿlab and others say angels had witnessed the jinn’s corruption and bloodshed, so they asked whether the new successor would follow the jinn’s way.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says jinn preceded Adam, corrupted the earth and shed blood; God sent angels who killed them and drove survivors to sea islands and mountain tops, then made Adam and his descendants successors.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says jinn preceded Adam, corrupted the earth and shed blood; God sent angels who killed them and drove survivors to sea islands and mountain tops, then made Adam and his descendants successors.

positions.position: خليفة and إمام overlap in use but differ: a khalifa succeeds a predecessor, while an imam leads and is to be followed and obeyed.
positions.reasons: TABRISI (author): خليفة and إمام overlap in use but differ: a khalifa succeeds a predecessor, while an imam leads and is to be followed and obeyed.

positions.position: A khalifa succeeds another and takes that one's place; Razi illustrates this with verses about successors on earth.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): A khalifa succeeds another and takes that one's place; Razi illustrates this with verses about successors on earth.

positions.position: One view takes the successor to be Adam, with his descendants, rather than Adam himself, intended by the prediction of corruption.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): One view takes the successor to be Adam, with his descendants, rather than Adam himself, intended by the prediction of corruption.

positions.position: If they are asking to remain in heaven rather than have a human vicegerent on earth, God says their welfare lies in being in heaven, not on earth.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): If they are asking to remain in heaven rather than have a human vicegerent on earth, God says their welfare lies in being in heaven, not on earth.

positions.position: Some exegetes, whom al-Qurtubi attributes to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and all interpreters, take the khalifa to mean Adam alone.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (ابن مسعود وابن عباس وجميع أهل التأويل): Some exegetes, whom al-Qurtubi attributes to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and all interpreters, take the khalifa to mean Adam alone.

positions.position: Ibn Jarir says a ruler is called khalifa because he succeeds his predecessor and takes charge in his place.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (ابن جرير): Ibn Jarir says a ruler is called khalifa because he succeeds his predecessor and takes charge in his place.

positions.position: One explanation supplies a description of the appointed successor's future conduct; otherwise the angels would have had no basis to predict corruption, and the remaining text confirms the omission.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (قيل): One explanation supplies a description of the appointed successor's future conduct; otherwise the angels would have had no basis to predict corruption, and the remaining text confirms the omission.

positions.position: An unattributed gloss says God's undisclosed knowledge concerned Iblis and the purpose for which the successor was created.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (author): An unattributed gloss says God's undisclosed knowledge concerned Iblis and the purpose for which the successor was created.

positions.position: God preserves the world through a single pole-like khalīfa in each age: Adam began the succession and Jesus will end it.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): God preserves the world through a single pole-like khalīfa in each age: Adam began the succession and Jesus will end it.

positions.position: The seeker should show humility before God, His caliphs, shaykhs, and scholars, avoiding ego and displays of knowledge; one pursuing annihilation should not admire the self.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): The seeker should show humility before God, His caliphs, shaykhs, and scholars, avoiding ego and displays of knowledge; one pursuing annihilation should not admire the self.

positions.position: The author explains the need for a vicegerent by the recipient's dense bodily nature and God's transcendence; under the divine order, an intermediary with both transcendent and attached aspects receives and transmits emanation.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): The author explains the need for a vicegerent by the recipient's dense bodily nature and God's transcendence; under the divine order, an intermediary with both transcendent and attached aspects receives and transmits emanation.

positions.position: As a locus of divine majesty and beauty, the vicegerent can manifest both; corruption and bloodshed are effects of majesty, while the angels left the unremarkable effects of beauty unmentioned.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): As a locus of divine majesty and beauty, the vicegerent can manifest both; corruption and bloodshed are effects of majesty, while the angels left the unremarkable effects of beauty unmentioned.

positions.position: Successors will carry out the same assigned duty, as expressed in the statement that God made people successors on earth.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): Successors will carry out the same assigned duty, as expressed in the statement that God made people successors on earth.

positions.position: The account's meaning is the distilled substance of extensive interpretations transmitted from the Companions and Successors.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (ashâb-ı kirâm ve tâbiîn): The account's meaning is the distilled substance of extensive interpretations transmitted from the Companions and Successors.

positions.position: The angels infer that an earthly successor must be numerous and socially organized, while embodied life and competition make corruption and bloodshed unavoidable.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): The angels infer that an earthly successor must be numerous and socially organized, while embodied life and competition make corruption and bloodshed unavoidable.

positions.position: Instead, God reveals a divine secret that angels cannot bear but the earthly successor can; this capacity makes up for the successor's corruption and bloodshed.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): Instead, God reveals a divine secret that angels cannot bear but the earthly successor can; this capacity makes up for the successor's corruption and bloodshed.

positions.position: Asad connects this reading to verses that call human beings khalaʾif al-arḍ, successors on earth.
positions.reasons: ASAD-NOTES (author): Asad connects this reading to verses that call human beings khalaʾif al-arḍ, successors on earth.

positions.position: Appointment as God's vicegerent is itself an honor, since the one entrusted with vicegerency must hold an elevated status.
positions.reasons: SAMARRAI-ASRAR (author): Appointment as God's vicegerent is itself an honor, since the one entrusted with vicegerency must hold an elevated status.

positions.position: Here and in 6:165, khalīfah suggests universal human inheritance and responsibility: all people are, in their inner reality, God’s vicegerents.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (author): Here and in 6:165, khalīfah suggests universal human inheritance and responsibility: all people are, in their inner reality, God’s vicegerents.

positions.position: Tabari says this may mean generations or a deputy judging by God's judgment.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Tabari says this may mean generations or a deputy judging by God's judgment.

positions.position: Tabari distinguishes God's deputy from Hasan's successive generations.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Tabari distinguishes God's deputy from Hasan's successive generations.

positions.position: One view says Adam is God’s deputy for establishing His law, signs of His oneness, and judgment among His creation.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (ابن مسعود ومجاهد): One view says Adam is God’s deputy for establishing His law, signs of His oneness, and judgment among His creation.

positions.position: Another view, attributed to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi, makes Adam God's deputy judging accountable creatures; 38:26 supports it.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (ابن مسعود وابن عباس والسدي): Another view, attributed to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi, makes Adam God's deputy judging accountable creatures; 38:26 supports it.

positions.position: Deputyship may arise from the principal's absence, need, or incapacity, or simply from the principal honoring a deputy despite none of those causes.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (Râgıb): Deputyship may arise from the principal's absence, need, or incapacity, or simply from the principal honoring a deputy despite none of those causes.

positions.position: A deputy's worth and honor are proportionate to the principal's honor and the degree of representation.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): A deputy's worth and honor are proportionate to the principal's honor and the degree of representation.

positions.position: The promise to establish a community as stewards is conditioned on faith and righteous conduct, supporting the interpretation of stewardship as service under God.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): The promise to establish a community as stewards is conditioned on faith and righteous conduct, supporting the interpretation of stewardship as service under God.

positions.position: Adam and his descendants exercise stewardship by living on God's earth in accordance with God's will and instructions.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): Adam and his descendants exercise stewardship by living on God's earth in accordance with God's will and instructions.

positions.position: Tabari rejects saying angels blamed the khalifa himself.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Tabari rejects saying angels blamed the khalifa himself.

turns_on: Whether succession is to God, earlier inhabitants, or earlier generations, and whether Adam or humanity is intended.

question: What work and authority does the khalīfa have?

positions.position: A khalifa is one entrusted to carry out an order on behalf of the one who commands.
positions.reasons: THALABI (author): A khalifa is one entrusted to carry out an order on behalf of the one who commands.

positions.position: Al-Hasan al-Basri takes خليفة as Adam's descendants, who succeed one another and Adam in upholding justice and cultivating earth.
positions.reasons: TABRISI (الحسن البصري): Al-Hasan al-Basri takes خليفة as Adam's descendants, who succeed one another and Adam in upholding justice and cultivating earth.

positions.position: A khalifa as God's deputy judges people; because judges are needed for disputes, announcing a successor implied future conflict.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): A khalifa as God's deputy judges people; because judges are needed for disputes, announcing a successor implied future conflict.

positions.position: The human vicegerent takes on God's traits, executes His command, governs creation, orders its affairs, and calls people to obedience.
positions.reasons: QASHANI (author): The human vicegerent takes on God's traits, executes His command, governs creation, orders its affairs, and calls people to obedience.

positions.position: Another view treats khalifa as the title of anyone entrusted with governing earth's people and overseeing their interests, as Caesar, Kisrā, and Tubbaʿ are royal titles.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Another view treats khalifa as the title of anyone entrusted with governing earth's people and overseeing their interests, as Caesar, Kisrā, and Tubbaʿ are royal titles.

positions.position: Al-Qurtubi suggests the angels may have understood khalifa as one who judges among people and restrains wrongs and violations.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (القرطبي): Al-Qurtubi suggests the angels may have understood khalifa as one who judges among people and restrains wrongs and violations.

positions.position: Khilāfa, like agency, is deputation in place of principal authority: taking another's place to some extent and representing that principal.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): Khilāfa, like agency, is deputation in place of principal authority: taking another's place to some extent and representing that principal.

positions.position: The vicegerent has no authority in his own right: he is a deputy charged to apply God's will, commands, and laws.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): The vicegerent has no authority in his own right: he is a deputy charged to apply God's will, commands, and laws.

positions.position: A vicegerent must represent God in all existential affairs, effects, laws, and governance; the flawed earthly being appears unfit to represent the perfectly pure God.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): A vicegerent must represent God in all existential affairs, effects, laws, and governance; the flawed earthly being appears unfit to represent the perfectly pure God.

positions.position: Ibn Jarir interprets the khalifa as God's deputy in judging among creation: Adam and those who obey God and rule justly; unjust corruption and bloodshed come from others.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (ابن جرير): Ibn Jarir interprets the khalifa as God's deputy in judging among creation: Adam and those who obey God and rule justly; unjust corruption and bloodshed come from others.

positions.position: Baghawi prefers that Adam is God's deputy on earth, charged with establishing His rulings and carrying out His commands.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI-FULL (author): Baghawi prefers that Adam is God's deputy on earth, charged with establishing His rulings and carrying out His commands.

positions.position: Ibn Masud says Adam is God’s deputy for judging servants by truth and His commands, a role continued by his descendants.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masud says Adam is God’s deputy for judging servants by truth and His commands, a role continued by his descendants.

positions.position: General stewardship is not exclusive to Adam; other verses explicitly extend this capacity and authority to all people.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): General stewardship is not exclusive to Adam; other verses explicitly extend this capacity and authority to all people.

positions.position: Human stewardship is limited to human nature and capacities; no creature can represent God, take God's place, or exercise God's authority.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): Human stewardship is limited to human nature and capacities; no creature can represent God, take God's place, or exercise God's authority.

question: What happened on earth before Adam?

positions.position: Jinn inhabited earth, corrupted it, and were defeated by angels before Adam
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Jinn first inhabited earth, angels heaven; envious, fighting jinn were defeated by a fiery host under Iblis. MUQATIL (author): Corruption means sins and bloodshed wrongfully, as earlier jinn did. TAB-FULL (author): Ibn Abbas reports jinn first corrupted earth and Adam succeeded them. ZAJJAJ (قيل): A people called jinn lived on earth, corrupted it and shed blood; God sent angels to drive them away, and the angels then inhabited earth. THALABI (المفسرون): Exegetes recount that jinn first worshipped on earth, then envy and aggression led them to fight and corrupt it. THALABI (المفسرون): An angelic force called jinn, led by Iblis, expelled the earlier jinn to mountains and sea islands and took over earth. THALABI (أكثر المفسرين): Most exegetes say the angels inferred human corruption by analogy with the earlier jinn, reasoning from the witnessed to the unseen. MAWARDI-FULL (author): Alternatively, the question form expresses an assertion; the angels inferred corruption from the jinn who had inhabited earth before. TABRISI (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas reports that jinn lived on earth, corrupted it and shed blood, were destroyed, and were replaced by Adam and his descendants. QURTUBI-FULL (أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب): Thaʿlab says the angels had seen jinn corrupt and shed blood on earth before Adam; God sent Satan with an angelic host to kill them and drive them to seas and mountains, so they asked whether the human successor would be like the jinn. NASAFI-FULL (author): Before Adam, jinn inhabited earth and corrupted it; angels expelled them to islands, seas, and mountaintops, then settled there. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (ابن عباس): A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says God first placed angels in heaven and jinn on earth; after the jinn corrupted and fought, Iblis led angels who expelled them and took earthly rule. IBNKATHIR-FULL (الضحاك عن ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, says jinn first inhabited earth and shed blood; God sent Iblis to defeat and drive them to remote places, then created Adam to succeed them. IBNKATHIR-FULL (الضحاك عن ابن عباس): Jinn had corrupted the earth before Adam’s descendants, and the angels compared the new beings with them. DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): In Ibn Abbas's account, jinn first inhabited earth and fought, shed blood, and were defeated by Iblis and an angel army, who drove them to islands and mountain edges. BURSEVI (author): After a long period, the jinn grew envious and oppressive, corrupted the earth, and killed; God sent the lowest-heaven angels under Iblis to defeat and expel them. STUDYQURAN (author): Prior jinn violence offers one possible explanation for the angels’ question about placing a corrupt, blood-shedding being on earth. STUDYQURAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): In the same report, jinn first inhabited earth and shed blood; God sent Iblīs with the al-ḥinn against them, driving them to islands and mountain edges, and Iblīs grew proud of the victory.

positions.position: Jinn lived on earth two thousand years before Adam and were expelled
positions.reasons: IBNABIHATIM (عبد الله بن عمرو): Abdullah ibn Amr says jinn inhabited earth two thousand years before Adam, spread corruption and bloodshed, and were driven to sea islands by an angelic force; this explains the angels' question. IBNKATHIR-FULL (عبد الله بن عمرو): A report says jinn lived on earth two thousand years before Adam, shed blood and caused corruption; angels drove them to sea islands, after which God announced Adam’s succession. DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): A report authenticated by al-Hakim says jinn inhabited earth for two thousand years before Adam, corrupted it and shed blood; angels drove them away, prompting their question about a successor.

positions.position: Angels were created Wednesday, jinn Thursday, and Adam Friday
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Rabi says angels fought rebellious jinn after their creation on Thursday. IBNABIHATIM (أبو العالية): Abu al-Aliya says angels were created Wednesday, jinn Thursday, and Adam Friday; rebellious jinn fought angels, so the angels compared humans' coming corruption and bloodshed to the jinn's.

positions.position: Al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas and also followed by al-Rabi b. Anas, says angels knew of the jinn who had lived on earth before Adam and asked whether later creatures would act like them; their question was
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (الضحاك عن ابن عباس والربيع بن أنس): Al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas and also followed by al-Rabi b. Anas, says angels knew of the jinn who had lived on earth before Adam and asked whether later creatures would act like them; their question was inquiry, not certainty.

positions.position: It is related that creatures lived on earth before Adam, caused corruption, and were destroyed by Iblīs and a company of angels sent by God.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (author): It is related that creatures lived on earth before Adam, caused corruption, and were destroyed by Iblīs and a company of angels sent by God.

positions.position: The alternative view is that the angels inferred the corruption from the condition of those who had lived before Adam.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (ابن عباس وأبي العالية ومقاتل): The alternative view is that the angels inferred the corruption from the condition of those who had lived before Adam.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas and al-Kalbi are cited for conjecture by analogy with the jinn who lived on earth before Adam.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (ابن عباس والكلبي): Ibn Abbas and al-Kalbi are cited for conjecture by analogy with the jinn who lived on earth before Adam.

positions.position: A fourth view from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā takes the question plainly: will this successor be like the earlier jinn who inhabited the earth?
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (أحمد بن يحيى): A fourth view from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā takes the question plainly: will this successor be like the earlier jinn who inhabited the earth?

positions.position: Ibn Umar is reported as giving the same account as Ibn Abbas about the earlier jinn and the angels' question.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (ابن عمر): Ibn Umar is reported as giving the same account as Ibn Abbas about the earlier jinn and the angels' question.

positions.position: The account says jinn, children of al-Jānn, were created from smokeless flame between heaven and earth and inhabited earth long before Adam.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): The account says jinn, children of al-Jānn, were created from smokeless flame between heaven and earth and inhabited earth long before Adam.

positions.position: Many commentators accept that jinn inhabited earth before human beings.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (many commentators): Many commentators accept that jinn inhabited earth before human beings.

positions.position: Jinn on earth resented being replaced because their worship duties were lighter.
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Jinn on earth resented being replaced because their worship duties were lighter.

positions.position: خليفة can mean a replacement for those who came before, here replacing the jinn.
positions.reasons: DAMGHANI (author): خليفة can mean a replacement for those who came before, here replacing the jinn.

positions.position: The enmity belongs to unbelieving jinn, not believers; unbelievers oppose human believers whether jinn or human. Another view makes it inherited without cause, and the author asks what caused Iblīs to refuse Adam's prostration.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): The enmity belongs to unbelieving jinn, not believers; unbelievers oppose human believers whether jinn or human. Another view makes it inherited without cause, and the author asks what caused Iblīs to refuse Adam's prostration.

positions.position: A further view says the addressees were Iblīs and angels who had fought rebellious jinn inhabiting the earth, driving them to mountain passes and islands.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (قيل): A further view says the addressees were Iblīs and angels who had fought rebellious jinn inhabiting the earth, driving them to mountain passes and islands.

positions.position: On this descendants interpretation, humans succeed earlier earth-dwellers, whether the jinn, Iblīs and his companions, or they succeed one another.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (قيل): On this descendants interpretation, humans succeed earlier earth-dwellers, whether the jinn, Iblīs and his companions, or they succeed one another.

positions.position: Some commentators analogized to predatory beasts that lived on earth before Adam, as in Genesis; Ibn ʿĀshūr likewise treats this as unnecessary.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (بعض المفسرين): Some commentators analogized to predatory beasts that lived on earth before Adam, as in Genesis; Ibn ʿĀshūr likewise treats this as unnecessary.

question: What is reported about Adam's formation and first acts?

positions.position: Adam's red and white clay from salt and fresh soil explains varied colors and faith among descendants.
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Adam's red and white clay from salt and fresh soil explains varied colors and faith among descendants.

positions.position: Adam's shaped clay lay forty years; Iblis entered and left the hollow body, boasting fire would overcome clay.
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Adam's shaped clay lay forty years; Iblis entered and left the hollow body, boasting fire would overcome clay.

positions.position: The spirit entered Adam's head, reached his navel and toes, and Adam sneezed and first praised God.
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): The spirit entered Adam's head, reached his navel and toes, and Adam sneezed and first praised God.

positions.position: Adam was made from clay of divine might and Muhammad's light.
positions.reasons: TUSTARI (author): Adam was made from clay of divine might and Muhammad's light.

positions.position: Ibn Sabit identifies corrupt blood-shedders as Adam's children.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Ibn Sabit identifies corrupt blood-shedders as Adam's children.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says Adam was formed from sticky clay, lay forty nights, and Iblis entered him.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Ibn Abbas says Adam was formed from sticky clay, lay forty nights, and Iblis entered him.

positions.position: In Ibn Abbas’s report, Adam’s haste is linked to human impatience; he praises God at a sneeze, Iblis refuses prostration from pride and is expelled, then Adam names things, while the angels disclaim unseen knowledge and
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (ابن عباس): In Ibn Abbas’s report, Adam’s haste is linked to human impatience; he praises God at a sneeze, Iblis refuses prostration from pride and is expelled, then Adam names things, while the angels disclaim unseen knowledge and God exposes Iblis’s concealed pride.

positions.position: Al-Suddi’s report from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Companions says Iblis ruled a heaven, grew proud, and angels were told the khalīfa’s descendants would corrupt, envy and kill; their question followed. The account then tells how
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح وابن عباس وابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي): Al-Suddi’s report from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Companions says Iblis ruled a heaven, grew proud, and angels were told the khalīfa’s descendants would corrupt, envy and kill; their question followed. The account then tells how angels collected multicolored clay despite earth’s pleas, explaining human diversity, and Adam was formed from it.

positions.position: Ibn Zayd relates that angels, afraid of hell, wondered whether they might disobey; God announced a human population of corruption, Adam’s knowledge proved his superiority, and Iblis refused to yield, citing fire versus clay.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (ابن زيد): Ibn Zayd relates that angels, afraid of hell, wondered whether they might disobey; God announced a human population of corruption, Adam’s knowledge proved his superiority, and Iblis refused to yield, citing fire versus clay.

positions.position: Ibn Ishaq says Adam was formed from earth and God’s hands for honor, lay forty years before ensoulment and became pottery-like without fire; he sneezed at ensoulment, angels prostrated, but proud, envious Iblis refused.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (ابن إسحاق): Ibn Ishaq says Adam was formed from earth and God’s hands for honor, lay forty years before ensoulment and became pottery-like without fire; he sneezed at ensoulment, angels prostrated, but proud, envious Iblis refused.

positions.position: The Adam narrative says clay was gathered from every region and left to ferment for forty mornings; the angels wondered what its destiny would be, then marveled at his fashioned form.
positions.reasons: QUSHAYRI (author): The Adam narrative says clay was gathered from every region and left to ferment for forty mornings; the angels wondered what its destiny would be, then marveled at his fashioned form.

positions.position: The Prophet said Adam was sixty cubits tall; the report is in the Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): The Prophet said Adam was sixty cubits tall; the report is in the Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

positions.position: Mention of earth implies a human made from clay; the angels wondered whether he would misuse delegated authority as if it were his own and cause corruption.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): Mention of earth implies a human made from clay; the angels wondered whether he would misuse delegated authority as if it were his own and cause corruption.

positions.position: The report says Adam’s clay body remained lifeless for forty years; Iblīs entered and taunted it, threatening to destroy or defy Adam if either gained power over the other.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): The report says Adam’s clay body remained lifeless for forty years; Iblīs entered and taunted it, threatening to destroy or defy Adam if either gained power over the other.

positions.position: In the account, God commands only the angels accompanying Iblīs to prostrate; Iblīs refuses, claiming superiority by age and greatness and contrasting his fire with Adam’s clay.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): In the account, God commands only the angels accompanying Iblīs to prostrate; Iblīs refuses, claiming superiority by age and greatness and contrasting his fire with Adam’s clay.

positions.position: The Quran’s other indication of this order of creation is 15:26–27: human beings were made from molded clay and jinn earlier from scorching fire.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (author): The Quran’s other indication of this order of creation is 15:26–27: human beings were made from molded clay and jinn earlier from scorching fire.

positions.position: Adam's spirit resisted entering the dark body and was told it would enter and leave unwillingly.
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Adam's spirit resisted entering the dark body and was told it would enter and leave unwillingly.

positions.position: Adam's early sitting illustrates human haste in 17:11.
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Adam's early sitting illustrates human haste in 17:11.

positions.position: When asked whether Adam was created for heaven or earth, Hasan answers that he was created for earth, citing this verse.
positions.reasons: IBNABIHATIM (الحسن): When asked whether Adam was created for heaven or earth, Hasan answers that he was created for earth, citing this verse.

positions.position: Al-Mufaḍḍal says the verse recalls God’s favor to Adam after the preceding reminder of what He created for people on earth.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI-FULL (المفضل): Al-Mufaḍḍal says the verse recalls God’s favor to Adam after the preceding reminder of what He created for people on earth.

positions.position: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī takes it as generations of Adam’s children succeeding one another in upholding right and cultivating earth.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI-FULL (الحسن البصري): Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī takes it as generations of Adam’s children succeeding one another in upholding right and cultivating earth.

positions.position: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd say God refers to Iblīs’s concealed pride and disobedience when commanded to prostrate to Adam.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI-FULL (ابن عباس وابن مسعود): Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd say God refers to Iblīs’s concealed pride and disobedience when commanded to prostrate to Adam.

positions.position: One account connects the verse to preceding favors: human creation and life, earthly things, heaven, then Adam and blessings to his descendants.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): One account connects the verse to preceding favors: human creation and life, earthly things, heaven, then Adam and blessings to his descendants.

positions.position: Iblīs took his success as proof of superiority and, in relation to Adam, incurred unbelief and disobedience.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (author): Iblīs took his success as proof of superiority and, in relation to Adam, incurred unbelief and disobedience.

positions.position: The other view says Adam succeeded earlier inhabitants of the earth.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (ابن عباس والحسن): The other view says Adam succeeded earlier inhabitants of the earth.

positions.position: The verse recounts Adam's creation and God's honoring of him, a general favor to all humanity and the third general blessing in this passage.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): The verse recounts Adam's creation and God's honoring of him, a general favor to all humanity and the third general blessing in this passage.

positions.position: Adam was sent to his own forty children, born as twenty pairs of a boy and a girl, whose descendants multiplied.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): Adam was sent to his own forty children, born as twenty pairs of a boy and a girl, whose descendants multiplied.

positions.position: The account of Adam’s offspring follows the verse about humanity’s single origin and its spouse.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The account of Adam’s offspring follows the verse about humanity’s single origin and its spouse.

positions.position: Biqai reads Adam’s public creation story as a manifest sign concealing the more elevated, privately understood account of Muhammad’s creat
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL (author): Biqai reads Adam’s public creation story as a manifest sign concealing the more elevated, privately understood account of Muhammad’s creation.

positions.position: The account places the Kursī inside the Throne, creates nested heavens and their inhabitants, and develops generated forms, spirits, bodies, and fitting sustenance.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (أهل الله): The account places the Kursī inside the Throne, creates nested heavens and their inhabitants, and develops generated forms, spirits, bodies, and fitting sustenance.

positions.position: Ibn al-Fāriḍ's verse voices the Muhammadan Reality: although outwardly a son of Adam, Muhammad bears an inner meaning that witnesses to his fatherhood.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (ابن الفارض): Ibn al-Fāriḍ's verse voices the Muhammadan Reality: although outwardly a son of Adam, Muhammad bears an inner meaning that witnesses to his fatherhood.

positions.position: This angel knew Adam's creation and rank because it inscribed all that would be on the Tablet, which experientially knew what the Pen wrote.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (السادة الصوفية): This angel knew Adam's creation and rank because it inscribed all that would be on the Tablet, which experientially knew what the Pen wrote.

positions.position: Divine vicegerency is shared by Adam's descendants; teaching the names deposits knowledge in humanity so its effects can unfold gradually and become actual through guidance.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): Divine vicegerency is shared by Adam's descendants; teaching the names deposits knowledge in humanity so its effects can unfold gradually and become actual through guidance.

positions.position: Qur'anic references to peoples succeeding earlier peoples support the view that earthly vicegerency is general to humanity, not exclusive to Adam.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): Qur'anic references to peoples succeeding earlier peoples support the view that earthly vicegerency is general to humanity, not exclusive to Adam.

positions.position: One possible referent is earlier conscious beings who lived on earth, whom Adam and humanity succeeded.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): One possible referent is earlier conscious beings who lived on earth, whom Adam and humanity succeeded.

positions.position: Successful vicegerency requires authority to administer its domain and proven capacity; God gave humanity the earth, Adam's test showed his fitness, and the chooser knows the unseen.
positions.reasons: SAMARRAI-ASRAR (author): Successful vicegerency requires authority to administer its domain and proven capacity; God gave humanity the earth, Adam's test showed his fitness, and the chooser knows the unseen.

positions.position: Eve enters without an account of her origin; although primordial Adam represents all humanity, male and female, the Quran does not explain how this Adam becomes the first couple.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (author): Eve enters without an account of her origin; although primordial Adam represents all humanity, male and female, the Quran does not explain how this Adam becomes the first couple.

question: What is reported about Iblis's earlier status and hidden pride?

positions.position: Iblis envied or scorned Adam and refused God's command
positions.reasons: MUQATIL (author): Iblis envied Adam's form; angels promised obedience, while Iblis privately resolved to disobey and mislead. TAB-FULL (مجاهد): Mujahid also says God knew Iblis concealed pride and would refuse to prostrate to Adam. WAHIDI-BASIT (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas and most commentators say angels compared Adam's descendants with corrupting jinn; God knew Iblis's pride and delusion, and angels later admitted ignorance when unable to name things. TABRISI (ابن عباس وابن مسعود): One view is that God knows Satan's concealed pride, vanity, and disobedience when ordered to prostrate to Adam. DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Iblis belonged to a group called jinn among the angels, was made from scorching fire, and was named al-Harith; other angels were from light and jinn from flame. MUQATIL (author): Iblis's boast and plan for Adam's descendants are linked to 34:20 and 17:62, excepting a few believers.

positions.position: Iblis held authority over earth or heaven and became proud
positions.reasons: WAHIDI-BASIT (author): The account says God had given Iblis dominion over earth, the lower heaven, and the gardens’ treasuries; he worshipped in these places, grew proud, and God disclosed his arrogance before announcing a successor on earth. BAGHAWI-FULL (author): God gave Iblis rule over earth, the lowest heaven, and the Garden treasury; his worship across these places led him to pride and the belief that he was God's most honored angel. BURSEVI (author): The narrative gives Iblis the name ʿAzāzīl and describes his rule over earth, the lowest heaven, and Paradise's treasury; he became proud of God's favors and imagined himself most honored. QURTUBI-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn ʿAbbas says Iblis grew arrogant after being honored as heaven's treasurer, assumed his rank made him superior, and scorned Adam's disobedience; the angels did not know Iblis's contrary inner state.

positions.position: Iblis became proud after defeating the jinn
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Ibn Abbas's account identifies Iblis as al-Harith of al-Hinn and describes the jinn's defeat and his hidden pride. TAB-FULL (author): The account continues: angels prostrate except proud Iblis, who is expelled; Adam names the creatures, the angels acknowledge they know only what God taught, and God reveals the pride Iblis concealed. DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Iblis became proud after defeating the jinn, while God knew the arrogance in his heart that the angels could not see.

positions.position: He calls the angels’ question a lapse and conjecture about the unseen; they were shown their error, repented and disclaimed unseen knowledge, while God exposed Iblis’s hidden arrogance.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): He calls the angels’ question a lapse and conjecture about the unseen; they were shown their error, repented and disclaimed unseen knowledge, while God exposed Iblis’s hidden arrogance.

positions.position: Al-Ṭabarī says this report’s opening differs from the earlier Ibn Abbas account, while its ending agrees in the angels’ admission of ignorance and disclosure of Iblis’s pride.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Al-Ṭabarī says this report’s opening differs from the earlier Ibn Abbas account, while its ending agrees in the angels’ admission of ignorance and disclosure of Iblis’s pride.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says God knew that Iblis's heart concealed arrogance and self-delusion unknown to the angels.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says God knew that Iblis's heart concealed arrogance and self-delusion unknown to the angels.

positions.position: God's answer points to Iblis's hidden arrogance, unknown to the angels, and reproaches their universal claim about themselves when some among them would disobey.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): God's answer points to Iblis's hidden arrogance, unknown to the angels, and reproaches their universal claim about themselves when some among them would disobey.

positions.position: Mujahid says God knew Iblis would disobey and created him for that disobedience.
positions.reasons: THALABI (مجاهد): Mujahid says God knew Iblis would disobey and created him for that disobedience.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says what God knew included Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey and his pride.
positions.reasons: WAHIDI-BASIT (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says what God knew included Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey and his pride.

positions.position: What God knew and the angels did not was Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey.
positions.reasons: WAHIDI-WAJIZ (author): What God knew and the angels did not was Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey.

positions.position: A force of angels called jinn, the keepers of the gardens, led by Iblis, drove the earthly jinn into mountains, valleys, and islands, then occupied earth.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI-FULL (author): A force of angels called jinn, the keepers of the gardens, led by Iblis, drove the earthly jinn into mountains, valleys, and islands, then occupied earth.

positions.position: Another explanation is that an angel among them, Iblis, will disobey God.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI-FULL (قيل): Another explanation is that an angel among them, Iblis, will disobey God.

positions.position: God may be revealing that Iblis is among the angels, with envy, pride, and hypocrisy in his heart.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): God may be revealing that Iblis is among the angels, with envy, pride, and hypocrisy in his heart.

positions.position: Repel Satan's harm by examining proofs, dispelling doubts, avoiding innovation and error, restraining desires, performing obedience, and avoiding major sins.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): Repel Satan's harm by examining proofs, dispelling doubts, avoiding innovation and error, restraining desires, performing obedience, and avoiding major sins.

question: Does the verse require appointing an imam?

positions.position: Al-Asamm says appointment is not obligatory if the community performs pilgrimage and jihad, acts fairly, distributes public funds, and applies legal penalties.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (الأصم): Al-Asamm says appointment is not obligatory if the community performs pilgrimage and jihad, acts fairly, distributes public funds, and applies legal penalties.

positions.position: The Rafidites say reason makes appointment obligatory, with revelation only confirming this.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (الرافضة): The Rafidites say reason makes appointment obligatory, with revelation only confirming this.

positions.position: If a small faction could deny necessary knowledge, established facts about Baghdad and far China could also be denied.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): If a small faction could deny necessary knowledge, established facts about Baghdad and far China could also be denied.

positions.position: Al-Qurtubi and others infer that appointing an imam is obligatory to settle disputes, defend the oppressed, enforce penalties and deter indecencies, since necessary duties require an imam.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (القرطبي وغيره): Al-Qurtubi and others infer that appointing an imam is obligatory to settle disputes, defend the oppressed, enforce penalties and deter indecencies, since necessary duties require an imam.

positions.position: Reason neither obligates or forbids nor makes things good or bad; appointment is obligatory by revelation, not reason.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): Reason neither obligates or forbids nor makes things good or bad; appointment is obligatory by revelation, not reason.

question: How is an imam appointed?

positions.position: The report of ʿUbada forbids disputing authority except upon clear unbelief for which there is proof from God; Muslim transmits it.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (النبي): The report of ʿUbada forbids disputing authority except upon clear unbelief for which there is proof from God; Muslim transmits it.

positions.position: An absta
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): An abstainer with an excuse is excused, while an unexcused person may be compelled so the Muslims do not divide.

positions.position: A duty to obey one named imam would require the whole community to know him; neither reason nor transmission establishes a particular person.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): A duty to obey one named imam would require the whole community to know him; neither reason nor transmission establishes a particular person.

positions.position: Abu Dawud and Ab
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (أبو داود السجستاني وأبو حاتم الرازي): Abu Dawud and Abu Hatim argue the Ghadir report conflicts with the Prophet’s saying that four tribes are clients only of God and His Messenger.

positions.position: A third route is agreement of the people empowered to bind and loose in the imam's city; if no successor exists, their accepted choice binds Muslims elsewhere unless the imam openly manifests corruption.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): A third route is agreement of the people empowered to bind and loose in the imam's city; if no successor exists, their accepted choice binds Muslims elsewhere unless the imam openly manifests corruption.

positions.position: The Prophet says sincerity to God, adherence to the community, and counsel to rulers keep rancor from a believer's heart, and the Muslims' call encompasses those behind them.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (رسول الله): The Prophet says sincerity to God, adherence to the community, and counsel to rulers keep rancor from a believer's heart, and the Muslims' call encompasses those behind them.

positions.position: The author rejects al-Jubbaʾi's extra requirements: both sides accept two witnesses, while the additional number has no supporting proof.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The author rejects al-Jubbaʾi's extra requirements: both sides accept two witnesses, while the additional number has no supporting proof.

positions.position: Asked about a ruler who overcomes the country, Sahl al-Tustari says to obey him, pay what he claims as his due, refrain from denouncing or fleeing him, and keep entrusted religious secrets.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (سهل بن عبد الله التستري): Asked about a ruler who overcomes the country, Sahl al-Tustari says to obey him, pay what he claims as his due, refrain from denouncing or fleeing him, and keep entrusted religious secrets.

positions.position: Some of the author's colleagues say witnesses are not required for the imamate contract because no decisive revealed proof establishes that requirement.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (بعض أصحابنا): Some of the author's colleagues say witnesses are not required for the imamate contract because no decisive revealed proof establishes that requirement.

positions.position: Others require witnesses to prevent secret competing claims and ensuing disorder, and consider two witnesses sufficient.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (بعض أصحابنا): Others require witnesses to prevent secret competing claims and ensuing disorder, and consider two witnesses sufficient.

positions.position: The majority say an imam who becomes manifestly sinful after appointment loses office, because sin disables the duties for which the imamate exists.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (الجمهور): The majority say an imam who becomes manifestly sinful after appointment loses office, because sin disables the duties for which the imamate exists.

positions.position: Others say removal is permitted only for unbelief, abandoning prayer or its call, or abandoning a rule of the law; the supporting hadith begins in the next segment.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (آخرون): Others say removal is permitted only for unbelief, abandoning prayer or its call, or abandoning a rule of the law; the supporting hadith begins in the next segment.

positions.position: A report says the imams are the community's intercessors, so people should consider whom they choose for intercession.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): A report says the imams are the community's intercessors, so people should consider whom they choose for intercession.

positions.position: Qatada says God knew that Adam’s descendants would include prophets, messengers, righteous people and inhabitants of Paradise.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (قتادة): Qatada says God knew that Adam’s descendants would include prophets, messengers, righteous people and inhabitants of Paradise.

positions.position: Another view requires testimony for the imamate contract, with two witnesses sufficient.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (قيل): Another view requires testimony for the imamate contract, with two witnesses sufficient.

positions.position: Another Sunni group holds that the imamate may be established by an indication or allusion.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (آخرون من أهل السنة): Another Sunni group holds that the imamate may be established by an indication or allusion.

question: What qualifications must an imam have?

positions.position: The Companions agreed on Abu Bakr after Saqifa; the Ansar proposed one leader from each group, but were persuaded that Arabs accepted Quraysh.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The Companions agreed on Abu Bakr after Saqifa; the Ansar proposed one leader from each group, but were persuaded that Arabs accepted Quraysh.

positions.position: Proposed routes to recognizing an imam are prophetic designation, choice by qualified electors, or possession of the required qualities and self-assertion.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): Proposed routes to recognizing an imam are prophetic designation, choice by qualified electors, or possession of the required qualities and self-assertion.

positions.position: Imamis say the imam is known only through a prophetic text; al-Qurtubi accepts reasoned consideration and qualified consensus as routes.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (الإمامية): Imamis say the imam is known only through a prophetic text; al-Qurtubi accepts reasoned consideration and qualified consensus as routes.

positions.position: The imam has eleven conditions; the first is descent from Quraysh, whose supporting report continues in the next segment.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The imam has eleven conditions; the first is descent from Quraysh, whose supporting report continues in the next segment.

positions.position: One qualified member of the people of authority can conclude the imamate, against those who require a group; Umar's pledge of Abu Bakr was accepted by the companions, and contracts need no minimum number.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): One qualified member of the people of authority can conclude the imamate, against those who require a group; Umar's pledge of Abu Bakr was accepted by the companions, and contracts need no minimum number.

positions.position: Some count seizure by a qualified contender as a fourth route to the imamate, even without consultation or prior choice, once people pledge to him.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): Some count seizure by a qualified contender as a fourth route to the imamate, even without consultation or prior choice, once people pledge to him.

positions.position: Ibn Khuwayz Mandad says a qualified person who seizes authority without consultation or choice has a completed pledge once people give allegiance.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (ابن خويز منداد): Ibn Khuwayz Mandad says a qualified person who seizes authority without consultation or choice has a completed pledge once people give allegiance.

positions.position: The first condition is Qurayshi descent, supported by the report that leaders are from Quraysh; the author notes disagreement over it.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The first condition is Qurayshi descent, supported by the report that leaders are from Quraysh; the author notes disagreement over it.

positions.position: God's choosing Talut means selecting him and indicates lineage as a condition; the imam need not be infallible, know the unseen, be the best horseman or bravest, or belong only to Banu Hashim.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): God's choosing Talut means selecting him and indicates lineage as a condition; the imam need not be infallible, know the unseen, be the best horseman or bravest, or belong only to Banu Hashim.

positions.position: The imam must be fit to judge Muslims and be an independent jurist who can address cases without needing another's legal opinion; this is agreed.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The imam must be fit to judge Muslims and be an independent jurist who can address cases without needing another's legal opinion; this is agreed.

positions.position: He needs sound judgment and practical expertise in war, armies, frontier defense, protecting the community, restraining wrongdoing, and recovering victims' rights.
