positions.position: The Prophet said Adam was created after the afternoon prayer on Friday, in its final hour before night; Muslim alone reports this.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): The Prophet said Adam was created after the afternoon prayer on Friday, in its final hour before night; Muslim alone reports this.

positions.position: In that report, an angel could not say how long he had existed, only that God had created a star every 400,000 years and that many such stars had appeared since his creation.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (ملك): In that report, an angel could not say how long he had existed, only that God had created a star every 400,000 years and that many such stars had appeared since his creation.

positions.position: Razi says all prophets agree on the existence of angels, a matter of consensus among them, established by transmitted reports.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (الأنبياء عليهم السلام): Razi says all prophets agree on the existence of angels, a matter of consensus among them, established by transmitted reports.

positions.position: A tafsir report says the heavens hear revelation like a chain striking stone, become frightened, then ask what God said and answer that He said the truth.

positions.position: One explanation, reported from Ibn Abbas, is that Adam succeeded the jinn removed from earth before his arrival.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (ابن عباس): One explanation, reported from Ibn Abbas, is that Adam succeeded the jinn removed from earth before his arrival.

positions.position: The Prophet said a community is not purified if the weak person's right is not taken from the strong; Ibn Majah transmits it, meaning may God not purify it.

positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (author): The angels' report that people pray at dawn and afternoon is one explanation of God's statement that He knows what they do not.

positions.position: Some reports say ten thousand angels who asked were consumed by fire; al-Ālūsī judges this report incorrect.

positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (author): Ibn Ashur invokes the angels' dialogue as an earlier example of reported speech in dialogue while explaining the unobserved scene in 2:133.

positions.position: Jabir reports the Prophet's account of the first creation: the Prophet's light produces all good, is divided into stages creating the Throne, Kursi, pen, Tablet, Paradise, angels, sun, moon, and virtues; its drops create 124,000 prophetic

positions.position: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says many mutually reinforcing reports witness to the thesis already presented and warns against dismissing these traditions as Sufi fabrications.

positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (Ibn ʿAbbās): Ibn ʿAbbās’s report identifies Iblīs as al-Ḥārith, a custodian of Paradise and member of the angelic tribe al-ḥinn, created from smokeless fire unlike the angels created from light.

positions.reasons: ITQAN (ابن النقيب): Ibn al-Naqib and others broaden the examples to include creatures' reported speech, such as the angels, hypocrites, Jews, and Christians, and foreign-language material.

positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): A line of poetry shows malāʾik without the feminine tāʾ; the poet is not identified in this passage.

positions.reasons: JISHUMI (أبو هاشم): Asked why God does not prevent Satan, Abū Hāshim says prevention adds duty deserving greater reward, like increased appetite, and Satan's misleading has an effect.

positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): They do nothing except by God's revelation and command.

positions.position: Eight bearers carry the Throne and Kursi; the smaller Kursi exceeds all seven heavens, displaying their strength.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Eight bearers carry the Throne and Kursi; the smaller Kursi exceeds all seven heavens, displaying their strength.

positions.position: A single trumpet blast makes those in heaven and earth swoon, and the next revives them, showing immense power.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): A single trumpet blast makes those in heaven and earth swoon, and the next revives them, showing immense power.

positions.position: The opponent also cites the prohibition on declaring oneself pure in 53:32.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (المخالف): The opponent also cites the prohibition on declaring oneself pure in 53:32.

positions.position: The command statement is universal because each commanded act allows exception, which removes what otherwise falls within the statement.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): The command statement is universal because each commanded act allows exception, which removes what otherwise falls within the statement.

positions.position: Their status as honored servants who do not speak ahead of God and act by His command clears them of sin.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Their status as honored servants who do not speak ahead of God and act by His command clears them of sin.

positions.position: Their gloss clears God's essence of bodily attributes and His acts of blame and foolishness.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (المعتزلة): Their gloss clears God's essence of bodily attributes and His acts of blame and foolishness.

positions.position: Remembering God benefits and purifies the servant, not God; the homily likens the command to a loan that God, though rich, repays tenfold.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Remembering God benefits and purifies the servant, not God; the homily likens the command to a loan that God, though rich, repays tenfold.

positions.position: God needs no army, but promises to help the servant who helps him, although heaven and earth are already his armies.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): God needs no army, but promises to help the servant who helps him, although heaven and earth are already his armies.

positions.position: God needs no remembrance because all already remember him, yet remembers the servant who remembers him; he needs no service, since he is king and all creation prostrates, but brief service earns lasting rest.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): God needs no remembrance because all already remember him, yet remembers the servant who remembers him; he needs no service, since he is king and all creation prostrates, but brief service earns lasting rest.

positions.position: The terms are associated with swimming in water and traversing land, respectively, in the sense of going through and far away.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): The terms are associated with swimming in water and traversing land, respectively, in the sense of going through and far away.

positions.position: In essence, God is beyond possibility: denying possibility entails denying multiplicity, corporeality, accidents, opposites, and peers, affirming absolute unity and necessary existence.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): In essence, God is beyond possibility: denying possibility entails denying multiplicity, corporeality, accidents, opposites, and peers, affirming absolute unity and necessary existence.

positions.position: In attributes, God is free of ignorance and change, encompasses all knowables, and is able to do all that can be done.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): In attributes, God is free of ignorance and change, encompasses all knowables, and is able to do all that can be done.

positions.position: In acts, God neither seeks benefit nor avoids harm nor gains or loses perfection; he is independent of all existents and nonexistents and sovereign over their creation and annihilation.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): In acts, God neither seeks benefit nor avoids harm nor gains or loses perfection; he is independent of all existents and nonexistents and sovereign over their creation and annihilation.

positions.position: David says he cannot thank God, since he can reach gratitude for a blessing only through another blessing; God says recognizing this dependence is gratitude.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (داود): David says he cannot thank God, since he can reach gratitude for a blessing only through another blessing; God says recognizing this dependence is gratitude.

positions.position: Saʿid ibn Jubayr recounts that a hypocrite rebuffed a Muslim who reminded him to pray; ʿUmar struck him, and the Prophet told ʿUmar his anger was honor and his approval judgment.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (سعيد بن جبير): Saʿid ibn Jubayr recounts that a hypocrite rebuffed a Muslim who reminded him to pray; ʿUmar struck him, and the Prophet told ʿUmar his anger was honor and his approval judgment.

positions.position: One interpretation addresses God: we declare him purified, describing him with the loftiness and might that befit him.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): One interpretation addresses God: we declare him purified, describing him with the loftiness and might that befit him.

positions.position: Abu Muslim says they purify their deeds of sin so the deeds are sincerely for God.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (أبو مسلم): Abu Muslim says they purify their deeds of sin so the deeds are sincerely for God.

positions.position: Another interpretation is purifying the heart of attention to anything besides God until it is absorbed in the lights of knowing him.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Another interpretation is purifying the heart of attention to anything besides God until it is absorbed in the lights of knowing him.

positions.position: The Qur'anic phrasing uses singular agreement by form, while Arabic also allows plural agreement by meaning, as illustrated by clauses about listeners.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The Qur'anic phrasing uses singular agreement by form, while Arabic also allows plural agreement by meaning, as illustrated by clauses about listeners.

positions.position: The phrase may encompass everything that was, is, and will be.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The phrase may encompass everything that was, is, and will be.

positions.position: The ending in malaʾika can mark the feminine plural, like ṣalādimah.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): The ending in malaʾika can mark the feminine plural, like ṣalādimah.

positions.position: Alternatively, the ending intensifies the sense, like ʿallāma and nassāba.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI-FULL (author): Alternatively, the ending intensifies the sense, like ʿallāma and nassāba.

positions.position: They overlooked that appetite and anger, disciplined by reason, yield chastity, courage, resisting desire, and justice; the human composite also enables grasping particulars, inventing crafts, and bringing nature’s potential benefits into actuality, the purpose of succession.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): They overlooked that appetite and anger, disciplined by reason, yield chastity, courage, resisting desire, and justice; the human composite also enables grasping particulars, inventing crafts, and bringing nature’s potential benefits into actuality, the purpose of succession.

positions.position: In 46:21, ‘remember the brother of ʿĀd when he warned his people’ means remember the event at that time: the event is omitted and its ظرف stands in its place.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): In 46:21, ‘remember the brother of ʿĀd when he warned his people’ means remember the event at that time: the event is omitted and its ظرف stands in its place.

positions.position: The segment attributes a reading of إني to the Hijazis and Abu ʿAmr.
positions.reasons: NASAFI-FULL (الحجازيون وأبو عمرو): The segment attributes a reading of إني to the Hijazis and Abu ʿAmr.

positions.position: Abu Hayyan calls that division a good interpretation, analogous to a collective quotation whose different statements belong to different groups.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Abu Hayyan calls that division a good interpretation, analogous to a collective quotation whose different statements belong to different groups.

positions.position: The earlier grammarians maintain that أفعل always carries a comparative sense, and Abu Hayyan endorses their position.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (النحويون المتقدمون): The earlier grammarians maintain that أفعل always carries a comparative sense, and Abu Hayyan endorses their position.

positions.position: Abu al-Abbas regards comparative-free use of أفعل as productive, while the cited grammarian says the sounder rule is to limit it to attested usage.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (أبو العباس): Abu al-Abbas regards comparative-free use of أفعل as productive, while the cited grammarian says the sounder rule is to limit it to attested usage.

positions.position: Another explanation is God’s complete knowledge of outward and inward matters, subtle and evident, near and distant, good and bad, across changing conditions and times.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (قول غير مسمى): Another explanation is God’s complete knowledge of outward and inward matters, subtle and evident, near and distant, good and bad, across changing conditions and times.

positions.position: Another explanation contrasts God’s knowledge, gained without acquisition, inquiry, reflection, or thought, with human knowledge.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (قول غير مسمى): Another explanation contrasts God’s knowledge, gained without acquisition, inquiry, reflection, or thought, with human knowledge.

positions.position: Grammarians disagree whether دم follows فَعْل with a quiescent middle radical or فَعَل with it open.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): Grammarians disagree whether دم follows فَعْل with a quiescent middle radical or فَعَل with it open.

positions.position: The Prophet says the deeds of night are raised to God before day, and the deeds of day before night.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): The Prophet says the deeds of night are raised to God before day, and the deeds of day before night.

positions.position: Ibn Ishaq interprets the words as a commitment not to disobey God or do anything He dislikes.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR-FULL (محمد بن إسحاق): Ibn Ishaq interprets the words as a commitment not to disobey God or do anything He dislikes.

positions.position: The Qur'an was not collected as a codex during the Prophet's life while revelation continued; Abu Bakr and the Companions compiled it after his death, then Uthman copied and dispatched codices.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (author): The Qur'an was not collected as a codex during the Prophet's life while revelation continued; Abu Bakr and the Companions compiled it after his death, then Uthman copied and dispatched codices.

positions.position: Delaying the person praised or blamed can emphasize the intended focus: نعم الرجل زيد is stronger than placing Zayd first.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (author): Delaying the person praised or blamed can emphasize the intended focus: نعم الرجل زيد is stronger than placing Zayd first.

positions.position: تضمين can also mean inserting another speaker's words into one's discourse to reinforce meaning or shape composition; Zarkashi calls this ibdaʿ.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (author): تضمين can also mean inserting another speaker's words into one's discourse to reinforce meaning or shape composition; Zarkashi calls this ibdaʿ.

positions.position: The author suggests Abū ʿAmr meant low frequency in the Qurʾān by few letters; recurrence matters, and Abū ʿAmr may also have weighed defectiveness and the received transmission.
positions.reasons: NASHR (author): The author suggests Abū ʿAmr meant low frequency in the Qurʾān by few letters; recurrence matters, and Abū ʿAmr may also have weighed defectiveness and the received transmission.

positions.position: The phrase about being dead, then made alive, dying, and being revived can be attached to an implied command to remember these events; the beginning already lets the thoughtful infer the return.
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL (author): The phrase about being dead, then made alive, dying, and being revived can be attached to an implied command to remember these events; the beginning already lets the thoughtful infer the return.

positions.position: Humanity was made for lasting life, not extinction: God created the cosmos for people, as provision, means, and support for their preservation and development.
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL (author): Humanity was made for lasting life, not extinction: God created the cosmos for people, as provision, means, and support for their preservation and development.

positions.position: Biqai describes two levels of discourse, a general one and a higher, more particular one that yields increasingly elevated meanings.
positions.reasons: BIQAI-FULL (author): Biqai describes two levels of discourse, a general one and a higher, more particular one that yields increasingly elevated meanings.

positions.position: Abu Malik says every Qur'anic statement introduced by “when” refers to something that has occurred.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (أبو مالك): Abu Malik says every Qur'anic statement introduced by “when” refers to something that has occurred.

positions.position: Al-Dahhak says every occurrence of “made” in the Qur'an means “created.”
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (الضحاك): Al-Dahhak says every occurrence of “made” in the Qur'an means “created.”

positions.position: “Major” idgham has a moving first letter in the pair, whether the letters are identical, alike in articulation, or near in articulation or quality; several explanations are given for its name.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): “Major” idgham has a moving first letter in the pair, whether the letters are identical, alike in articulation, or near in articulation or quality; several explanations are given for its name.

positions.position: Among the ten imams, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala is especially associated with major idgham; it is also reported from al-Hasan al-Basri, al-A'mash, Ibn Muhaysin, and others.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): Among the ten imams, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala is especially associated with major idgham; it is also reported from al-Hasan al-Basri, al-A'mash, Ibn Muhaysin, and others.

positions.position: Its purpose is ease of pronunciation, though many prominent works on readings do not mention it.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): Its purpose is ease of pronunciation, though many prominent works on readings do not mention it.

positions.position: Mutamathilain share articulation and quality; mutajanisain share articulation but differ in quality; mutaqaribain are close in articulation or quality.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): Mutamathilain share articulation and quality; mutajanisain share articulation but differ in quality; mutaqaribain are close in articulation or quality.

positions.position: Idgham among identical letters occurs across seventeen letters; the verse's “we glorify You” is one example, as are other cited letter pairs.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): Idgham among identical letters occurs across seventeen letters; the verse's “we glorify You” is one example, as are other cited letter pairs.

positions.position: The conditions include matching in writing and usually meeting across two words; exceptions include مناسككم and ما سلككم, while pronoun tāʾ, a doubled first letter, and tanwin prevent idgham.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): The conditions include matching in writing and usually meeting across two words; exceptions include مناسككم and ما سلككم, while pronoun tāʾ, a doubled first letter, and tanwin prevent idgham.

positions.position: Qāf assimilates into kāf after a vowel and also in one word before mīm; kāf assimilates into qāf after a vowel, except when its preceding letter is still.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): Qāf assimilates into kāf after a vowel and also in one word before mīm; kāf assimilates into qāf after a vowel, except when its preceding letter is still.

positions.position: To sanctify for God means to purify.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (ابن عباس): To sanctify for God means to purify.

positions.position: Tadmin has four senses: using a word for another whose meaning it contains; implying a meaning without naming it; linking post-rhyme wording to the rhyme; and embedding another's speech to reinforce meaning or structure.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): Tadmin has four senses: using a word for another whose meaning it contains; implying a meaning without naming it; linking post-rhyme wording to the rhyme; and embedding another's speech to reinforce meaning or structure.

positions.position: Ibn Abi al-Isba says he found Qur'anic examples only in two places, each incorporating a passage from the Torah or Gospel: “life for life” and “Muhammad is God's messenger.”
positions.reasons: ITQAN (ابن أبي الإصبع): Ibn Abi al-Isba says he found Qur'anic examples only in two places, each incorporating a passage from the Torah or Gospel: “life for life” and “Muhammad is God's messenger.”

positions.position: The intended first human and his spouse are Adam and Hawwa; her name is written long because she was created from a living person.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (author): The intended first human and his spouse are Adam and Hawwa; her name is written long because she was created from a living person.

positions.position: Bursevī also says even the wisest man, finest mount, and most devout woman need a counselor, a whip, and a spouse respectively.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): Bursevī also says even the wisest man, finest mount, and most devout woman need a counselor, a whip, and a spouse respectively.

positions.position: The Prophet warns against gloating over a brother’s misfortune, since God may relieve him and test the one who gloats.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (النبي): The Prophet warns against gloating over a brother’s misfortune, since God may relieve him and test the one who gloats.

positions.position: Israelites made the same entitlement argument against Talut; God answered that kingship rests on divine choice and superiority in knowledge and physique, not wealth.
positions.reasons: BURSEVI (author): Israelites made the same entitlement argument against Talut; God answered that kingship rests on divine choice and superiority in knowledge and physique, not wealth.

positions.position: The Pen has 360 teeth and the Intellect 360 manifestations; each yields 360 classes of general knowledge unfolded on the Tablet, beginning with nature beneath the soul.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (أهل الله): The Pen has 360 teeth and the Intellect 360 manifestations; each yields 360 classes of general knowledge unfolded on the Tablet, beginning with nature beneath the soul.

positions.position: After recounting favors to earlier people, God follows with a universal blessing and complete honor; beneficence to the ancestor also benefits the descendant.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): After recounting favors to earlier people, God follows with a universal blessing and complete honor; beneficence to the ancestor also benefits the descendant.

positions.position: Some treat the word as hollow from lāka yalūku; the feminine ending is explained either as feminine plural or as an intensifier.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (بعض): Some treat the word as hollow from lāka yalūku; the feminine ending is explained either as feminine plural or as an intensifier.

positions.position: They identify one addressed angel as al-Rūḥ, the highest Pen, or First Intellect, a mirror of the divine Essence and the axis of the worlds and their inhabitants.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (السادة الصوفية): They identify one addressed angel as al-Rūḥ, the highest Pen, or First Intellect, a mirror of the divine Essence and the axis of the worlds and their inhabitants.

positions.position: The comprehensive divine Name makes vicegerency and cosmic governance possible, while God alone truly acts; the author notes the difficulty of this doctrine and its many deniers.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): The comprehensive divine Name makes vicegerency and cosmic governance possible, while God alone truly acts; the author notes the difficulty of this doctrine and its many deniers.

positions.position: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Mawṣilī chose the circumstantial reading; al-Ālūsī says respect restrains him from commenting on that choice and ultimately upholds the explanation he has set out.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (علاء الدين الموصلي): ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Mawṣilī chose the circumstantial reading; al-Ālūsī says respect restrains him from commenting on that choice and ultimately upholds the explanation he has set out.

positions.position: Al-Khazraji compares the two-part response to the divided alternative “Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided.”
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): Al-Khazraji compares the two-part response to the divided alternative “Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided.”

positions.position: Al-Alusi prefers explaining the unspecified knowledge by God's statement that He knows the unseen of the heavens and earth.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): Al-Alusi prefers explaining the unspecified knowledge by God's statement that He knows the unseen of the heavens and earth.

positions.position: The lām in “for You” can mark devotion: the act is done for God and sincerely for His sake.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): The lām in “for You” can mark devotion: the act is done for God and sincerely for His sake.

positions.position: He invokes the maxim that a person seeking judicial office should not be appointed to it.
positions.reasons: ELMALILI (author): He invokes the maxim that a person seeking judicial office should not be appointed to it.

positions.position: He distinguishes conventional knowledge, defined by society and era, from true knowledge that perfects people and reveals beneficial realities; both can confer mastery and partly overlap.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (author): He distinguishes conventional knowledge, defined by society and era, from true knowledge that perfects people and reveals beneficial realities; both can confer mastery and partly overlap.

positions.position: Human virtues may emerge from paired defects: courage, for example, lies between recklessness and cowardice.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (author): Human virtues may emerge from paired defects: courage, for example, lies between recklessness and cowardice.

positions.position: Al-Khattabi says Qur'anic rhetoric is miraculous because it combines three levels of eloquence, excluding the disapproved hybrid, to achieve both grandeur and sweetness.
positions.reasons: BINTSHATI-IJAZ (الخطابي): Al-Khattabi says Qur'anic rhetoric is miraculous because it combines three levels of eloquence, excluding the disapproved hybrid, to achieve both grandeur and sweetness.

positions.position: Al-Khattabi was an early observer of fine semantic distinctions among Qur'anic terms often treated as synonyms, including knowledge and knowing, praise and thanks, and emancipation and manumission.
positions.reasons: BINTSHATI-IJAZ (الخطابي): Al-Khattabi was an early observer of fine semantic distinctions among Qur'anic terms often treated as synonyms, including knowledge and knowing, praise and thanks, and emancipation and manumission.

positions.position: People must recognize their opportunities and blessings as God's property, entrusted for a purpose and condition, and use them according to God's will and approval.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): People must recognize their opportunities and blessings as God's property, entrusted for a purpose and condition, and use them according to God's will and approval.

positions.position: An a fortiori argument says that if mortal conscious beings exist, immortal ones can also exist, and intelligent beings in the lower world make such beings in the nobler heavens all the more plausible.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): An a fortiori argument says that if mortal conscious beings exist, immortal ones can also exist, and intelligent beings in the lower world make such beings in the nobler heavens all the more plausible.

positions.position: The Qur'an mentions the trumpet to be blown at the beginning of the resurrection and revival.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): The Qur'an mentions the trumpet to be blown at the beginning of the resurrection and revival.

positions.position: The commentary finds two explanations more reasonable, closer to reality, and more consistent with the narrative style.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): The commentary finds two explanations more reasonable, closer to reality, and more consistent with the narrative style.

positions.position: Tabari rejects Ibn Ishaq's meaning of inhabiting and cultivating.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (author): Tabari rejects Ibn Ishaq's meaning of inhabiting and cultivating.

positions.position: The reading that a virtuous woman is ‘a man in meaning’ is rejected: it conflicts with the moon example and makes the couplet self-contradictory.
positions.reasons: JURJANI-ASRAR (author): The reading that a virtuous woman is ‘a man in meaning’ is rejected: it conflicts with the moon example and makes the couplet self-contradictory.

positions.position: A proposed meaning is God’s knowledge of Iblīs’s concealed disobedience, but the author rejects it because Iblīs has not yet been mentioned.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): A proposed meaning is God’s knowledge of Iblīs’s concealed disobedience, but the author rejects it because Iblīs has not yet been mentioned.

positions.position: Because the passage can mean zakāt, the author rejects its abrogation.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): Because the passage can mean zakāt, the author rejects its abrogation.

positions.position: Choosing worldly or later punishment is incoherent: repentance should have been offered, as it is even to lifelong polytheists and prophet-persecutors.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Choosing worldly or later punishment is incoherent: repentance should have been offered, as it is even to lifelong polytheists and prophet-persecutors.

positions.position: Abū Ḥayyān counts
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Abū Ḥayyān counts eight such analyses and says the Qurʾān should be kept clear of them.

positions.position: Bint al-Shati rejects the implication that Qur'anic passages occupy lower eloquence levels: inimitability reaches the highest level, and one sura need not combine all three because the challenge concerns a single sura.
positions.reasons: BINTSHATI-IJAZ (author): Bint al-Shati rejects the implication that Qur'anic passages occupy lower eloquence levels: inimitability reaches the highest level, and one sura need not combine all three because the challenge concerns a single sura.
